title: OpenAI says AI agents solved centuries-old mathematical problem in 88 hours
key_facts: OpenAI announced an internal system produced a proposed solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a Clay Millennium Prize problem.
Precisely, it built a finite-time singularity for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with a smooth external force, one route allowed by the Clay formulation; it does not settle the unforced question.
OpenAI's report: about 10,000 concurrent agents, 2.7 million messages, roughly 130 billion output tokens.
Agents reached the proposed solution about 88 hours in, followed by 17 hours of Lean formalization and verification.
Mathematicians Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpoge (Anthropic) had earlier made progress on the related Euler equations, using Claude and OpenAI Codex.
Buckmaster asked if OpenAI's model had seen their drafts; OpenAI says his Codex prompts from the prior two months could not have influenced the system.
A credit dispute followed over how a joint paper would be authored.
quote_evidence: According to OpenAI's official report, the Navier-Stokes effort involved on the order of 10,000 concurrent AI agents, 2.7 million messages and roughly 130 billion output tokens.
It does not settle the better-known question of whether the unforced equations always remain smooth.
So based on the evidence currently available, there is no basis for saying OpenAI trained on their unpublished proof or copied their private research.
why_it_matters_hint: If it holds, thousands of agents working in parallel can produce checkable research results, but the human groundwork and credit are disputed.
event_date: Announcement before 30 Sep 2026 (exact date not stated); agents' run about 88 hours plus 17 hours of checking
